spans.title: I Do Indeed Come from Scotland
spans.blurb: A nervous young Scot finally meets the literary giant he reveres, and his very first sentence hands the famous wit a perfect opening.

spans.title: The Dinner with Jack Wilkes
spans.blurb: A determined young matchmaker of enemies tricks a great moralist into dining with the scandalous politician he loathes, then watches nervously from across the table.

books.pairNote: Two separate anecdotes from the same friendship, years apart; neither repeats or flattens the other.

spans.title: The Swineherd
spans.blurb: A scorned prince disguises himself as a palace pigkeeper and sets an unusual price on his ingenious toys: kisses from the princess who rejected him.

spans.title: Devotion
spans.blurb: At a late supper party, a young man follows a beautiful, ailing courtesan from the table and offers her the one thing she refuses to believe in.

spans.title: Down Upper Swandam Lane
spans.blurb: Sent to fetch a friend home from a riverside opium den at midnight, a doctor feels a pluck at his sleeve and a whisper: walk past, then look back.

spans.title: The Ungloved Hand
spans.blurb: A young reporter arrives at a chateau, stares at his host's gloved hands, and refuses to shake until he sees what the gloves conceal.

spans.title: The Man at the Desk
spans.blurb: Midnight at a guarded chateau: a young reporter climbs a ladder to a lit window and finds an intruder calmly writing at the victim's desk.
spans.spoilerNote: It hints that the attacked woman knows her assailant and is shielding him, a question the full book unwinds slowly.

books.pairNote: An arrival scene and a midnight stakeout from different points in the investigation; no shared text or shared payoff.

spans.title: The Turning Key
spans.blurb: Two watchers keep a silent vigil over a sleeping general when a key turns softly in the lock and an arm reaches through the dark.

spans.title: The Lamp and the Tree
spans.blurb: A poet waits rigid as a statue beneath a street lamp at night, determined to end an argument about order and anarchy once and for all.

spans.title: The Lobster and the Bombs
spans.blurb: In a greasy beershop, a poet orders champagne and lobster for his guest, then politely warns him not to be alarmed if the table begins to turn.

books.pairNote: Back-to-back scenes from the same night; the story picks up soon after the short's ominous closing line, but neither repeats the other's punch.

spans.title: The Harp in the Danish Camp
spans.blurb: A defeated king lays down his sword, takes up an old harp, and walks unarmed into the firelit camp of the invaders to sing for them.

spans.title: Noman and the Cyclops
spans.blurb: Trapped in a man-eating giant's cave, a cunning captain sharpens a beam of olive wood, pours strong wine, and gives a very careful answer about his name.

spans.title: A Hand in the Dark
spans.blurb: Letting himself into a friend's dark apartment at night, a man reaches for the light switch and closes his fingers over warm flesh.

spans.title: Morning in the Police Court
spans.blurb: A ragged burglar caught hiding in a coat closet stands before the judge, while the volunteer lawyer defending him grows strangely uneasy.

books.pairNote: A courtroom scene and a later break-in scuffle; separate incidents with separate shocks.
